6	the way we work changes, change it here.
7	
8	## What this repo is
9	
10	A reference scaffold for **agentic engineering**: the files, gates, and context
11	that make AI-written code consistent and enterprise-grade. TypeScript + React is
12	just the runnable carrier. The scaffolding is the point (see the root
13	`README.md` and [`NORTH_STAR.md`](NORTH_STAR.md)).
14	
15	## Run it
16	
17	```bash
18	pnpm install          # install dependencies (Node ≥ 22.18, pnpm)
19	pnpm setup:agents     # install the external agentic toolkit (one time)
20	pnpm dev              # run web (http://localhost:5173) and api (:3001) together; Vite proxies /trpc
21	pnpm lint:policy      # ESLint: policy, React hooks, and React Compiler rules
22	pnpm arch:check       # architecture gate, structure check, diagram freshness, API report freshness
23	pnpm arch:diagram     # regenerate docs/architecture/roles.mmd and each result's architecture.mmd
24	pnpm api:report       # regenerate each package's etc/*.api.md after an intended export change
25	pnpm verify           # the full local gate suite (typecheck → biome → eslint → react doctor → fallow → architecture → tests → build)
26	pnpm e2e              # playwright test: every spec in each result's web/e2e/, with its api and web servers
27	```
28	
29	## Run a Todo trial
30	
31	The orchestrator runs each Todo trial; an agent inside a trial builds its
32	result from the prompt alone. Run trials one at a time, from the checkout
33	that keeps the evidence, at the scaffold revision every trial shares
34	([ADR 0034](decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)):
35	
36	```bash
37	pnpm trial --trial 1 --scaffold <rev> --trials-root <dir> --dry-run   # print the plan and the exact claude argv
38	pnpm trial --trial 1 --scaffold <rev> --trials-root <dir>             # clone, run one fresh session, check, record
39	git fetch <dir>/todo-01-<stamp>/repo trial/todo-01:trial/todo-01         # keep the result branch
40	```
41	
42	Pass `--agent codex` for a fresh Codex exec session (default: `claude`).
43	Pass `--task /absolute/path/task.json` for a task file; a task with a target
44	repository pins its own revision and needs no `--scaffold`. Task-local prompts
45	and acceptance commands stay outside the clone. External tasks use `land: patch`
46	and can set an absolute `evidenceDir` to keep private evidence outside this repo.
47	See [ADR 0048](decisions/0048-trial-tasks-and-codex.md). Todo Codex ids are
48	`todo-codex-01..03`; compare keeps Todo runs and proves baselines per agent.
49	
50	The run writes `docs/trials/todo-01.json`, the agent's stream as
51	`todo-01.stream.jsonl` with secrets redacted (and `todo-01.patch` when it
52	fails), and prints its workdir. Fetch the result branch, then remove the
53	workdir before the next trial; the harness refuses to start while one
54	remains. Pass `--retry` only after a failure from before the agent started.
55	
56	Each trial's commands use a private temp and cache folder inside its
57	workdir, and bubblewrap (`bwrap`) mounts that temp folder over `/tmp`, so the
58	agent sees only its own `/tmp` files. Install bubblewrap first: a trial fails
59	before its agent starts when `bwrap` fails to run. No time limit
60	applies. Stop a trial with Ctrl-C, and read how long it took from
61	`run.durationMs` and `run.agentDurationMs` in its record
62	([ADR 0038](decisions/0038-trial-isolation-and-no-time-limit.md)).
63	
64	After the three trials, merge each passed result branch with `git merge --no-ff`,
65	commit every record, stream and patch, and run
66	`node tooling/trial/compare.mjs` to write `docs/trials/comparison.md`: the
67	full pass count, the shared baseline and each difference between the runs,
68	classified against the spec freedoms of
69	[ADR 0035](decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md) and
70	[ADR 0037](decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md).
71	
72	## The golden rules
73	
74	1. **Read before you write.** Architecture, conventions, the Definition of Done,
75	   the glossary, and ADRs live in this folder.
76	2. **Follow the patterns; copy the templates.** New files come from
77	   [`templates/`](templates/). Consistency is the deliverable.
78	3. **Behaviour is defined by the E2E map**, each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`
79	   (for example `apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`), not by the implementation.
80	   Add behaviour there first. A feature's PRD in `docs/prd/` states its intent
81	   and links each behaviour to the test that proves it.
82	4. **When a gate fails, fix the cause.** Keep every gate and its config as it
83	   is; the checks below enforce this.
84	5. **Done means the gates are green.** Report a task complete once
85	   `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass; see
86	   [`project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md`](project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md).
87	6. **PRs carry proof.** Complete the pull request template and follow
88	   [`project/PR_QUALITY.md`](project/PR_QUALITY.md) before opening a PR or
89	   marking it ready.
90	7. **Change rules in the open.** When a constraint is wrong, propose an ADR in
91	   [`decisions/`](decisions/) and change the rule there.
92

1	# Architecture
2	
3	> This is the anchor for **showcase #2**: agent-written code must follow the
4	> patterns described here. When asked to verify or review work, an agent checks
5	> the change against this document first.
6	
7	## The shape
8	
9	The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
10	([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):
11	
12	- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference
13	  result lives in `apps/` (`@repo/web`, `@repo/api`). Each generated trial
14	  result lives in `showcase/<id>/` with the same shape.
15	- `packages/ui` (`@repo/ui`) holds the UI primitives every result renders with.
16	- `tooling/results.mjs` (`listResults`) is the one place that discovers
17	  results: the reference first, then each `showcase/<id>` that has both
18	  `web/package.json` and `api/package.json`, sorted by id.
19	
20	The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
21	joins every gate with no config entry of its own.
22	
23	The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
24	api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.
25	
26	```
27	apps/
28	├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
29	│   ├── src/
30	│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider
31	│   │   ├── App.tsx                      # mounts the routes; holds no business logic
32	│   │   ├── index.css
33	│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
34	│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
35	│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient

42	│   │   │       ├── GreetingPage.tsx     # the page: composes the route's components

57	    │   ├── router.ts                    # appRouter and the AppRouter type

62	    │           ├── procedures.ts        # validates input, delegates to application

65	    │           ├── integrations.ts      # storage and every effect (the greeting has none)
66	    │           └── *.test.ts
67	    ├── etc/

69	packages/ui/                             # @repo/ui, react as its only peer

79	└── api/                                 # @<id>/api: package.json, src/, etc/
80	```
81	
82	## Roles
83	
84	[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
85	a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
86	`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any value import the table does not allow,
87	and `coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. A
88	role may import types (`import type`, `export type … from`) from any other
89	role ([ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)).
90	Inline `type` specifiers count too, as in `import { type Greeting }`, when
91	every specifier carries one. Fallow reads a plain `import { Greeting }` as a
92	value import even when the file uses `Greeting` only as a type, so write
93	`import type`.
94	A slice of a role still imports nothing from a sibling slice. Paths below are
95	relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).
96	
97	| Role | Files | May import |
98	| --- | --- | --- |
99	| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
100	| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role |
101	| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
102	| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` |
103	| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role |
104	| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` |
105	| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role |
106	| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` |
107	| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` |
108	| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role |
109	| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` |
110	
111	Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
112	and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
113	folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
114	role.
115	
116	The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
117	shows every role and every value direction the rules allow. Each result has
118	its own generated diagram,
119	[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
120	`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
121	resolve to. An edge is dashed where the contract allows its pair for types
122	only. A type-only import along a direction that also allows values draws
123	solid, because Fallow's graph records no import kind; the trial comparison
124	reads the sources and counts that edge as type-only. Both come from
125	`pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.
126	
127	## Result structure
128	
129	`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
130	included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):
131	
132	- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
133	  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
134	  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
135	  role.
136	- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
137	  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
138	  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
139	  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
140	  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
141	  rather than link it.
142	- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
143	  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
144	  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
145	  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
146	  lists only external ones.
147	- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
148	- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
149	- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
150	  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
151	  pragma.
152	
153	## The api file roles
154	
155	| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
156	| --- | --- | --- |
157	| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
158	| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
159	| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing by value: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
160	| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. Application calls it. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
161	| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |
162	
163	The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:
164	
165	```ts
166	// apps/api/src/router.ts
167	import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
168	import { router } from './trpc.ts';
169	
170	export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
171	export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
172	```
173	
174	Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
175	the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
176	with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
177	because Vite resolves it.
178	
179	## The web state model
180	
181	| State | Owner | Where |
182	| --- | --- | --- |
183	| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
184	| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema)), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
185	| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |
186	
187	A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
188	mutation or form of its own.
189	
190	Any web role may name an api type with `import type` from `@repo/api`. The api
191	client is the only web module that wires the tRPC client and imports its
192	packages, `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query`. Everything else
193	reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:
194	
195	```ts
196	// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
197	const trpc = useTrpc();
198	const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));
199	
200	// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
201	const queryClient = useQueryClient();
202	const mutation = useMutation(
203	  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
204	    onSuccess: () =>
205	      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
206	  }),
207	);
208	```
209	
210	Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
211	per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
212	hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:
213	
214	```tsx
215	function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
216	  const view = render(
217	    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
218	      <GreetingPage />
219	    </TestApiProvider>,
220	  );
221	  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
222	}
223	```
224	
225	A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
226	`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.
227	
228	## The rules (and why)
229	
230	Each rule fails a check on a seeded violation in a committed test
231	(`tooling/architecture/boundaries.test.ts`, `scripts/eslint-policy.test.ts`,
232	`tooling/architecture/typescript.test.ts`). The check's message names the fix.
233	
234	| Rule | Why | Enforced by | Proved by |
235	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
236	| Routes own page composition. | One place per page keeps navigation readable. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
237	| Sibling slices stand alone: a route imports no other route, a feature no other feature. | Each slice changes without breaking its siblings. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` for every result; Fallow child zones for the `apps/web` routes | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
238	| Every file belongs to one role and one slice. | Extra layers and loose files hide structure. | Fallow `coverage.requireAllFiles`; `policy/slice-isolation` for a loose file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm lint:policy` |
239	| A package reaches another only by its package name. | Public exports are the only contract. | `policy/slice-isolation` (relative import out of the package) | `pnpm lint:policy` |
240	| A module is imported through its `index.ts`. | The public surface is a deliberate, reviewed list. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports`; API reports | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm api:check` |
241	| Procedures validate their input with Effect Schema. | Data from the network is untrusted until parsed. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
242	| Procedures delegate to application logic. | Transport stays thin; logic stays testable. | Fallow `api-procedures` value-imports only `api-trpc`, `api-application` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
243	| The domain is pure, and application knows no tRPC. | Rules test as plain functions. | Fallow `api-domain`; `contract/domain-pure`, `contract/application-without-trpc`; `tsconfig.domain.json` (no Node types) | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`, `pnpm typecheck` |
244	| Effects run only in integrations or the api composition root. | One place to swap storage or IO. | `contract/effects-in-integrations`, `contract/io-effects-in-integrations`, `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
245	| The web reaches the api only by type: `import type` of the router type. | The bundle carries no server code. | Fallow `allowTypeOnly` (a value import of `api-app` fails); the `types`-only export of `@repo/api`; `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client`, `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
246	| UI primitives hold no business logic. | The kit stays reusable across results. | Fallow `ui` imports nothing by value; `contract/ui-without-logic` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
247	| One React component per file. | One file, one reason to change. | ESLint `policy/one-component-per-file` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
248	| State, server state and form state live in `use*` hooks. | Components render; hooks wire. | ESLint `policy/state-and-effects-in-hooks` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
249	| Forms validate with Effect Schema. | One schema language across web and api. | ESLint `policy/form-uses-effect-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
250	| Web code has the DOM and no Node; api code has no DOM and only erasable syntax; domain code has neither. | The browser has no Node, and Node strips types and runs the source as is. | `tsconfig.json` (web, ui), `tsconfig.api.json` and `tsconfig.domain.json` over `tsconfig.base.json` | `pnpm typecheck` |
251	| Behaviour is defined by each result's E2E specs. | The product contract survives refactors. | Playwright, one project per result | `pnpm e2e` |
252	
253	`contract/<id>` is a rule in
254	[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc),
255	which Fallow loads as a rule pack and reports as an error. The behaviour map
256	is each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, for example
257	[`apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`](../../apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts); see
258	[ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-behaviour-mapped-with-e2e.md). Each feature's PRD
259	in `docs/prd/`, such as [`docs/prd/greeting.md`](../../docs/prd/greeting.md),
260	states its intent and links each behaviour to the test that proves it
261	([ADR 0045](../decisions/0045-prds-state-intent-and-link-their-specs.md)).
262	
263	## Architecture checks
264	
265	`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
266	file:
267	
268	- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
269	  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
270	  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
271	- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
272	  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
273	  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
274	  differs from a fresh run.
275	- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
276	  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
277	  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
278	  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
279	  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
280	  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.
281	
282	`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
283	point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
284	with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
285	included.
286	
287	## Showcase results
288	
289	A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
290	([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
291	harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
292	lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.
293	
294	- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
295	  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
296	- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
297	  nothing from another result.
298	- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
299	  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
300	- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
301	  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
302	- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
303	  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
304	- Its structure, public API, dependencies, component boundaries and
305	  conventions are compared with every other run, failed runs included, in
306	  `docs/trials/comparison.md`, which `node tooling/trial/compare.mjs`
307	  generates ([ADR 0035](../decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md)). Keep each
308	  difference inside a spec freedom that ADR or
309	  [ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)
310	  lists: a type-only import between roles, and dropping a re-export a gate
311	  flagged, are among them.
312	
313	## What this template intentionally omits
314	
315	The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
316	are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
317	inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
318	in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.
319	
320	## How to extend
321	
322	Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
323	reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.
324	
325	### Add an api feature
326	
327	1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
328	   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
329	   storage or any effect.
330	2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
331	   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
332	   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
333	3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
334	   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.
335	
336	### Add a procedure
337	
338	1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
339	   `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`.
340	2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
341	   delegate to one application function.
342	3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
343	   `procedures.test.ts`.
344	
345	### Add a route
346	
347	1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
348	   `index.ts` that exports the page.
349	2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
350	   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
351	   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
352	3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
353	4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
354	5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
355	   runs every spec in that folder.
356	
357	### Add a web feature
358	
359	Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
360	is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
361	import it through its `index.ts`.
362	
363	### Finish
364	
365	1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
366	2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
367	   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
368	3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

# Architecture

> This is the anchor for **showcase #2**: agent-written code must follow the
> patterns described here. When asked to verify or review work, an agent checks
> the change against this document first.

## The shape

The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):

- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference
  result lives in `apps/` (`@repo/web`, `@repo/api`). Each generated trial
  result lives in `showcase/<id>/` with the same shape.
- `packages/ui` (`@repo/ui`) holds the UI primitives every result renders with.
- `tooling/results.mjs` (`listResults`) is the one place that discovers
  results: the reference first, then each `showcase/<id>` that has both
  `web/package.json` and `api/package.json`, sorted by id.

The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
joins every gate with no config entry of its own.

The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.

```
apps/
├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider
│   │   ├── App.tsx                      # mounts the routes; holds no business logic
│   │   ├── index.css
│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient
│   │   │   ├── TestApiProvider.tsx      # the same providers over typed in-memory handlers
│   │   │   ├── testApiHandlers.ts       # TestApiHandlers, one handler per procedure path
│   │   │   ├── useTestApiClients.ts
│   │   │   └── index.ts                 # public surface
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   │   └── greeting/                # one folder per route, kebab-case
│   │   │       ├── GreetingPage.tsx     # the page: composes the route's components
│   │   │       ├── GreetingForm.tsx     # one component per file

## Roles

[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any value import the table does not allow,
and `coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. A
role may import types (`import type`, `export type … from`) from any other
role ([ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)).
Inline `type` specifiers count too, as in `import { type Greeting }`, when
every specifier carries one. Fallow reads a plain `import { Greeting }` as a
value import even when the file uses `Greeting` only as a type, so write
`import type`.
A slice of a role still imports nothing from a sibling slice. Paths below are
relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).

| Role | Files | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role |
| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role |
| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` |
| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role |
| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` |
| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` |
| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role |
| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` |

Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
role.

The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
shows every role and every value direction the rules allow. Each result has
its own generated diagram,
[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
resolve to. An edge is dashed where the contract allows its pair for types
only. A type-only import along a direction that also allows values draws
solid, because Fallow's graph records no import kind; the trial comparison
reads the sources and counts that edge as type-only. Both come from
`pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.

## Result structure

`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):

- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
  role.
- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
  rather than link it.
- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
  lists only external ones.
- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
  pragma.

## The api file roles

| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing by value: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. Application calls it. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |

The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:

```ts
// apps/api/src/router.ts
import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
import { router } from './trpc.ts';

export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
```

Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
because Vite resolves it.

## The web state model

| State | Owner | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema)), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
mutation or form of its own.

Any web role may name an api type with `import type` from `@repo/api`. The api
client is the only web module that wires the tRPC client and imports its
packages, `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query`. Everything else
reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:

```ts
// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
const trpc = useTrpc();
const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));

// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const mutation = useMutation(
  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
  }),
);
```

Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:

```tsx
function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
  const view = render(
    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
      <GreetingPage />
    </TestApiProvider>,
  );
  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
}
```

A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

## Architecture checks

`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
file:

- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
  differs from a fresh run.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.

`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
included.

## Showcase results

A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.

- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
  nothing from another result.
- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
- Its structure, public API, dependencies, component boundaries and
  conventions are compared with every other run, failed runs included, in
  `docs/trials/comparison.md`, which `node tooling/trial/compare.mjs`
  generates ([ADR 0035](../decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md)). Keep each
  difference inside a spec freedom that ADR or
  [ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)
  lists: a type-only import between roles, and dropping a re-export a gate
  flagged, are among them.

## What this template intentionally omits

The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.

## How to extend

Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.

### Add an api feature

1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
   storage or any effect.
2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.

### Add a procedure

1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
   `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`.
2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
   delegate to one application function.
3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
   `procedures.test.ts`.

### Add a route

1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
   `index.ts` that exports the page.
2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
   runs every spec in that folder.

### Add a web feature

Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
import it through its `index.ts`.

### Finish

1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

# Conventions

Each convention below names the check that enforces it. The error message of
each check names the fix. The judgment calls at the end are the conventions no
check can decide; reviewers hold those. When in doubt, copy the reference
feature.

## Enforced conventions

The ESLint rules and the Biome naming override run on every package source:
`{apps,packages}/*/src/**` and `showcase/*/*/src/**`.

| Convention | Enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| Folders under a package `src/` are kebab-case (`name-input`). | ESLint `policy/folder-names` |
| Each folder under a package `src/` is named for its role (`name-input`, `api-client`). Code in a catch-all folder (`utils`, `helpers`, `lib`, `common`, `shared`, `misc`) moves into the slice that uses it, or into `@repo/ui` when it is a shared UI primitive. | ESLint `policy/role-named-folders` |
| Each test sits beside its subject as `<Name>.test.ts(x)` or `<Name>.<kind>.test.ts(x)` (`GreetingPage.a11y.test.tsx` beside `GreetingPage.tsx`), outside any `__tests__/` folder. A source file with no test is fine; coverage thresholds decide what is tested. | ESLint `policy/test-beside-subject` |
| Identifiers: `camelCase` functions and variables, `PascalCase` types and components, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for true configuration constants. | Biome `style/useNamingConvention` |
| File names are camelCase, PascalCase, or the name of their export. | Biome `style/useFilenamingConvention` |
| A component or hook lives in the file of the same name (`GreetingForm.tsx`, `useGreeting.ts`). | ESLint `policy/file-matches-export` |
| One React component per file. | ESLint `policy/one-component-per-file` |
| Function components only. | ESLint `react-doctor/prefer-function-component` |
| `useState`, `useReducer`, effects, TanStack Query hooks (`useQuery`, `useSuspenseQuery`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `useMutation`) and React Hook Form hooks (`useForm`, `useFieldArray`) run only inside a named custom `use*` hook. | ESLint `policy/state-and-effects-in-hooks` ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-local-state-inside-custom-hooks.md)) |
| `useForm` takes `resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `standardSchemaResolver` from `@hookform/resolvers/standard-schema` and `Schema` from `effect`. | ESLint `policy/form-uses-effect-schema` |
| Every api procedure input is `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))` with `Schema` from `effect`. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` |
| Derived values are computed during render instead of copied into state by an effect. | ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, `react-doctor/no-derived-state`, `react-doctor/no-mirror-prop-effect` |
| Functions defined inside a component start with `handle` (`handleGreet`). | ESLint `policy/handler-names` |
| Callback props start with `on` (`onGreet`). | ESLint `policy/callback-prop-names` |
| Page components (`<Name>Page`) live in `src/routes/<route-name>/`. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` zone |
| Each file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` sits in a slice folder, and a slice imports no sibling slice. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation`, Fallow child zones for `apps/web` |
| A relative import stays inside its package; other packages are imported by name (`@repo/ui`). | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` |
| Another module imports a route, feature or api feature only through its `index.ts`: `./routes/greeting` in the web, `./features/greeting/index.ts` in the api. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports` |
| Every relative import in an api package names its `.ts` extension (`./application.ts`). | `pnpm typecheck` (`tsconfig.api.json`, `NodeNext`) and Node at runtime |
| Api code uses only erasable TypeScript syntax and sees no DOM; web code has the DOM and no Node globals. | `pnpm typecheck` (`tsconfig.api.json` with `erasableSyntaxOnly`; `tsconfig.json` with the DOM libs and no Node types) |

| Imports follow the role table in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md). | Fallow boundaries (`pnpm arch:gate`) |

| --- | --- |

| `contract/application-without-trpc` | `application.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`; procedures map errors to tRPC. |
| `contract/effects-in-integrations` | `fetch`, `self.fetch`, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync` and `Effect.runFork` run only in `integrations.ts` or the api `server.ts` and `router.ts`. |
| `contract/io-effects-in-integrations` | Network, storage, process and shell work runs only there too. |
| `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | Node IO modules (`fs`, `http`, `net`, `child_process`) are imported only there too. |
| `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client` | `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query` are imported only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
| `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | Web and ui code imports `@trpc/server` only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
| `contract/ui-without-logic` | `packages/ui` imports no query, form, schema or tRPC library. |

## State ownership

| State | Owner | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` from the api client, with `queryOptions` or `mutationOptions` | `use<Name>.ts` in the route folder (`useGreeting.ts`) |
| Form state | React Hook Form with `standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))` and `defaultValues` | `use<Name>Form.ts` (`useGreetingForm.ts`) |
| Form schema | Effect Schema | `<name>FormSchema.ts` (`greetingFormSchema.ts`) |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

After a mutation, refresh the queries it changes in `onSuccess` with
`queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() })`.

## Api file roles

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `features/<name>/procedures.ts` | The feature router. Validates each input with `Schema.toStandardSchemaV1` and delegates to application. |
| `features/<name>/application.ts` | Use cases. Calls domain and integrations; knows no transport. |
| `features/<name>/domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. |
| `features/<name>/integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect. |
| `features/<name>/index.ts` | The public surface: the feature router. |

See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full role table and the
greeting reference.

## Judgment calls

- **Full words in identifiers.** Write `name` and `request`. The name is the
  cheapest documentation an agent has. Established acronyms such as E2E, CI,
  ADR, UI, IO, and URL are fine.
- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See
  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.
- **Validate data at an IO boundary.** Parse network, storage, and environment
  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect
  Schema. A type assertion is a claim, and validation is proof.
- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.

## Enforced commit and branch conventions

| Convention | Enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| Commits use Conventional Commits, `type(scope): subject`, lower case with no trailing period. | commitlint on `commit-msg` |
| PR titles use Conventional Commits. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
| Branches are `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`, for example `feat/greeting-trim-name`. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
| A new dependency arrives with a new ADR that names it. | `pnpm check:adr` in `pnpm verify` and CI |

## Commit judgment

- Write the subject in the imperative mood.
- Keep one logical change per commit, so the diff stays reviewable.
